why: Hands-on care can create comfort and make movement easier. Movement is how we rebuild function, confidence, tolerance, and capacity.

slides.title: Movement Rebuilds Function
slides.content: Movement is how your body rebuilds strength, tolerance, confidence, and function. You do not need the perfect exercise to begin.

slides.title: Treatment Opens an Opportunity
slides.content: Hands-on care can reduce pain, improve comfort, and make movement easier. That creates an opportunity to return to activity and build on the change.

slides.title: Use the Opportunity
slides.content: Walk, work, exercise, or return to ordinary activity in a way you can manage. Movement helps turn improved comfort into useful capacity.

slides.title: Start, Then Build
slides.content: Keep moving, start with what you can do, and build from there. Specific restrictions or guidance are added when your condition, goals, or response require them.

slides.title: Symptoms Are Information
slides.content: A symptom response is information—not an automatic damage report. Consider its intensity, duration, trend, and effect on function.

slides.title: Try this today
slides.content: Choose one ordinary activity you want treatment to make easier. Use today’s window of comfort to practise it at a level you can manage.
